# Senso-ji Temple (浅草寺)

> > Official website of Senso-ji, Tokyo's oldest Buddhist temple dedicated to Kannon (Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva), located in Asakusa since 628 CE.

Senso-ji (浅草寺) is a historic Buddhist temple founded during the reign of Empress Suiko, enshrining the sacred image of Kannon discovered in the Sumida River by the Hinokuma brothers. The temple serves as a major pilgrimage site and cultural landmark, offering worship services, religious amulets, and preserving centuries of Tokyo's spiritual heritage from the Edo period to present day.

## Key Topics

- Senso-ji Temple (浅草寺)
- Kannon worship (聖観世音菩薩)
- Asakusa Kannon
- Empress Suiko (推古天皇)
- Hinokuma brothers (檜前浜成・檜前竹成)
- Sumida River (隅田川)
- Kaminarimon Gate (雷門)
- Temple buildings and halls (影向堂, 淡島堂, 銭塚地蔵堂, 鎮護堂)
- Buddhist pilgrimage
- Edo period history
- Omamori (protective amulets)
- Tokyo's oldest temple
- Avalokitesvara Bodhisattva
- Temple festivals and monthly events
- Religious services and blessings

## Temple Overview

- [ASAKUSA KANNON SENSOJI (English)](https://www.senso-ji.jp/english/): English homepage for Senso-ji, Tokyo's oldest Buddhist temple in Asakusa
- [浅草寺公式サイト (Japanese Homepage)](https://www.senso-ji.jp/): Japanese homepage for Senso-ji Temple, official site of Asakusa Kannon
- [About Senso-ji (浅草寺を知る)](https://www.senso-ji.jp/about/): About Senso-ji: temple history, origins, and Kannon worship heritage

## Worship & Religious Services

- [Worship Guide (ご参拝)](https://www.senso-ji.jp/visit/): Worship guide: prayer services, rituals, blessings, and memorial services
- [Omamori & Amulets (お守り)](https://www.senso-ji.jp/charm/): Omamori charms and religious amulets available at Senso-ji Temple
